Wait substitution of hydroxyl with halogen: starting material has OH, product has halogen. In retrosynthesis, we break C-X to get C-O (leaving group). So the target molecule (product) contains C-X (alkyl halide). The precursors would be the alcohol (C-OH) and maybe HX? But here precursors are CNOC and benzoic acid, not typical.

Maybe the target molecule is "CNOC(=O)c1ccccc1" which is a carbamate of benzoic acid? That contains C-O bond (ester) linking CNOC group to benzoyl. The substitution could be converting the O of the carbamate to halogen? Not sure.
